subject: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@sumanalytics.com>, Priya Shah <priya@sumanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review

Thanks for the time earlier, Alex & Priya — good call. Quick recap and where we land from our side:  

- Goal: Meet Summit Analytics' 99th-pct latency SLOs for interactive analytics (target: <= 250ms for 95% of responses, 99th-pct <= 600ms) while supporting concurrent exploratory sessions (expected peak 650 concurrent users, estimated 4 requests/sec per user during bursts).
- Key constraints you shared: bursty traffic (analysts spin up model runs in parallel), streaming responses for large result sets (chunked tokens), and strict token-cost governance.

From Redwood:
- Baseline recommendation: reserve a Dedicated pool with a predictable throughput lane sized for sustained load of ~8k RPS aggregate and a burst window for up to 16k RPS for short periods (5–10m).
- Connection model: we recommend client-side pooling with 30 persistent HTTP/2 connections per region + per-connection multiplexing up to 50 parallel streams, yielding a safe concurrency envelope while keeping socket counts low.
- Rate limits: propose per-connection QPS cap of 60 QPS (soft), per-API-key sustained cap of 10k QPS (account-level) with a temporary negotiated burst multiplier (2x) for onboarding stress tests.

Action items (next steps):
1) Summit to share a 1-hour sample of production traffic (anonymized) or a synthetic trace so we can validate the 8k sustained / 16k burst assumptions.
2) Redwood to run a canary with streaming enabled (small dataset) and provide the streaming-latency-profile.pdf and conn-capacity-matrix.csv.
3) Ben to send an updated ratecard with a temporary burst addendum for the POC.
4) Agree on go/no-go criteria for the POC: 95% success under 8k sustained and tail-latency under 600ms at 16k burst for 5 minutes.

Attachments: conn-capacity-matrix.csv (proposed lanes), streaming-latency-profile.pdf (example output from similar customer).

Thanks — I put Ben and Marcus in the thread to own ratecard and bench artifacts. If this looks good I can circulate a short playbook and a DocuSign addendum for the temporary burst.

— Irene Choi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0147


From: Alex Mercer <alex@sumanalytics.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya@sumanalytics.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review

Thanks, Irene — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we generate the synthetic trace:  

1) When you say "per-connection multiplexing up to 50 parallel streams", is that an HTTP/2 stream limit we're free to exploit from our clients? Our current web tier uses keep-alive HTTP/1.1 across a fleet of edge nodes and the default browsers will only open 6 connections; we may need an edge proxy change.
2) For the "temporary negotiated burst multiplier (2x)", how does Redwood enforce fairness across other hosted tenants if customers use Hosted API vs Dedicated? We want guarantees that our burst won't throttle other critical jobs.

Also: we can produce a 60-minute anonymized trace (traffics.csv) by Monday — it will include per-session inter-request intervals and token counts. Would that be sufficient?

Alex
VP Product, Summit Analytics
alex@sumanalytics.com

On a related note, attaching one real incident from last quarter where ~300 concurrent analysts triggered a spike that doubled concurrency for ~8 minutes — I can include the metrics if helpful.
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@sumanalytics.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@sumanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review

Hi Alex — quick answers and a first-pass ratecard proposal.

1) HTTP/2 multiplexing: yes, we recommend using an edge proxy (envoy/nginx) or a small client pool that speaks HTTP/2 to Redwood endpoints. Browser-level limitations are expected; typical deployment is keep N persistent connections from each app server to Redwood (envoy handles connection reuse). The 50-streams figure is conservative for internal multiplexing.

2) Burst fairness: for Dedicated customers we isolate capacity to the reserved pool during the burst window. If Summit opts for Dedicated with a burst addendum we will carve temporary capacity exclusively for your account for the agreed burst window. For Hosted API customers, bursts are governed by global rate limits and we can't guarantee dedicated capacity without a committed contract.

Attached is redwood-ratecard-proposal-v2.xlsx with three options:
- Option A (POC): Dedicated small pool (baseline 8k RPS), 2x burst multiplier for 30 days, fixed monthly commit + usage overage pricing.
- Option B (Pilot): Start hosted but reserve a Dedicated warm-standby lane we can flip during tests (best-effort carve).
- Option C (Enterprise): Heavy reserved capacity with lower unit price and SLA-backed burst windows.

Technical suggestions for the POC:
- Start with 20–30 persistent connections per app-region, each capped at 40 concurrent streams.
- Use short-lived canary bursts (ramp 0→100%) over 5 minutes, test streaming chunking with a 1MB/response payload to validate chunk handling and tail latencies.

If that aligns I'll spin up the POC config and schedule a load window with our infra team.

— Ben
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachment stubs: redwood-ratecard-proposal-v2.xlsx (sheet: POC-options)

Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Ben. A few items from our side:  

- We'll generate the 60-minute anonymized trace and a short script that replays the inter-request timing (will post by Monday).
- The browser constraint is a thing — we'll likely adopt a small edge proxy pool to translate many browser clients into fewer persistent HTTP/2 connections to Redwood.
- We prefer Option A (POC Dedicated) assuming the burst addendum is contractually timeboxed (30 days) and there's a clearly defined rollback if we hit sustained oversubscription.

Priya and I are aligned to the test criteria. Can we get 3 preferred windows for the canary next week? Also please include any test credentials / test API key with limited scope.

Thanks — Alex

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@sumanalytics.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@sumanalytics.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Concurrency & connection pacing — capacity playbook review

Great — thanks Alex. Finalizing logistics:  

- Ben: can you upload the POC config and the temporary API key (scoped, expires in 10 days) to the shared playbook link and confirm the three windows? Prefer morning windows PST: Tue 9am, Wed 11am, Thu 8am.
- Marcus: please prep a short bench run that exercises both streaming and non-streaming paths and include token-budget telemetry in the CSV. Use the 1MB payload scenario Ben mentioned.
- Alex/Priya: please share the anonymized trace and the replay script by Monday EOD so we can pre-simulate.

I created a short one-page addendum (DocuSign link below) that formalizes the 30-day burst multiplier and the rollback terms; signing it will allow us to allocate the Dedicated burst lane for your POC. Link: https://app.docusign.com/transactions/1234ABCD

If all good I will schedule the canary and loop in infra on the morning of the window. Minimal paperwork so we avoid procurement delays: the addendum only covers the burst carve for the POC period.

— Irene
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.ai
